title: Retrieval strategies
task_statement: Choose a retrieval strategy for each query shape, and route live state to a tool. (Inference: wording from secondary sources)

components.name: Hybrid keyword and semantic retrieval
components.first_principle: Pick the matcher that fits the query shape, and merge the candidates from both matchers.

nodes.label: Metadata filter for source, date, and access

steps: Apply metadata filters to limit the pool to documents the user may read. (Inference)
Score the pool with keyword match for codes, names, and identifiers.
Score the pool with embedding similarity for paraphrased questions.
Merge both ranked lists with rank fusion. (Inference)
Send the merged candidates to a reranker when the list is long. (Inference)
pros: Keyword match finds exact codes that a vector match can miss. (Inference)
Embedding similarity finds passages that use different words from the question. (Inference)
Metadata filters limit results to allowed documents. (Inference)
cons: Two indexes need two refresh paths. (Inference)
The merge step needs a fusion rule for two ranked lists. (Inference)
Official pages describe no hybrid search feature. Not in source.
use_when: The corpus holds codes, SKUs, or names that a vector match misses. (Inference)
Users ask in plain words about text that uses exact identifiers. (Inference)
Access rules differ by user and must limit the candidate pool. (Inference)
do_not_use_when: All queries are exact codes, where keyword match alone fits. (Inference)
The corpus is small enough for full document context. (Inference)
The answer depends on live state, which needs a tool call instead. (Inference)

constraints.choice: Run both matchers in parallel, then merge the results. (Inference)
constraints.combination: Add a reranker only when the merged list is long. (Inference)

constraints.choice: Apply access filters before scoring, so users never see chunks they may not read. (Inference)
Keep a second index only when query shapes need the second matcher. (Inference)
constraints.combination: Use int8 output for embeddings to cut vector storage by 4x.

constraints.choice: Log which matcher produced each kept candidate. (Inference)
constraints.combination: Compare precision per matcher on a labeled set of questions. (Inference)

native_services.text: Not in source. The retrieval pages name no native platform service for keyword search.

components.exam_tie: D3.6. Expect a scenario with codes and paraphrases in the same corpus. The credited answer covers both matchers with a filter. (Inference)
components.trap: A single semantic index looks sufficient. Exact codes often fail to match in vector space, so the codes go unfound. (Inference)
components.decision_rule: Use keyword match for exact terms, semantic match for paraphrases, and filters for access. (Inference)
components.exam_tip: If the scenario names both codes and paraphrases, choose hybrid retrieval. (Inference)

components.name: Reranking candidates
components.first_principle: A reranker scores a candidate list again and reorders it for the query.
steps: Retrieve a wide candidate list from the index.
Send the query and the candidate documents to the reranker.
The reranker returns the documents in relevance order.
Keep the highest ranked passages for the model context.
Check recall at the retrieval stage when the answer is absent. (Inference)
pros: Rerankers return documents ranked by relevance to the query.
rerank-3 is recommended for most applications.
rerank-3-lite is optimized for latency and cost.
cons: A reranker adds a model call and extra latency. (Inference)
A reranker cannot return a document that retrieval did not return. (Inference)
Rerank pricing sits in MongoDB documentation, outside the Claude docs.
use_when: The answer appears in the candidates, but the order is wrong. (Inference)
Answer quality depends on the top few passages. (Inference)
do_not_use_when: Recall is low, because a reranker only reorders the list. (Inference)
The candidate list is already short and ordered well. (Inference)

constraints.choice: Use rerank-3-lite when latency and cost bind.
constraints.combination: Use rerank-3 when accuracy binds the decision.

constraints.choice: Keep each query and document set under the 32,000 token context length.
Rerank a shorter candidate list to cut calls and tokens. (Inference)
Track which candidates move into the top passages.
constraints.combination: Compare the top passages with the cited passages in each answer. (Inference)

native_services.text: Not in source. The embeddings page names a Voyage AI rerank call, not a native platform service.

components.exam_tie: D3.6. Expect a scenario where the right passage exists but ranks low. The credited answer adds a reranking stage. (Inference)
components.trap: A larger generation model looks like the fix for an absent answer. The answer was never in the candidate list, so no model can cite it. (Inference)
components.decision_rule: Add a reranker when the answer appears in the candidates but ranks low. (Inference)
components.exam_tip: If the answer is absent from the candidates, fix retrieval, not the reranker. (Inference)

components.name: Live state through a tool call
components.first_principle: Answer questions about current values with a tool call to the source system, not with an indexed snapshot.
steps: Classify each question as a document question or a live state question. (Inference)
Send live state questions to a tool that reads the source system.
Claude calls the tool when the request maps to the tool description.
Send document questions to the index and cite the passages.
Answer from the tool result, not from an older indexed copy. (Inference)
pros: A tool result reflects the source system at call time. (Inference)
Tool descriptions steer which tool Claude calls.
The index does not need a rebuild for each state change. (Inference)
cons: The tool needs authentication and a latency budget. (Inference)
A misrouted question still reads the old snapshot. (Inference)
The MCP connector requires a server reachable over HTTP.
use_when: Answers change faster than the index refresh cycle. (Inference)
The source system exposes a read tool for the needed fields. (Inference)
do_not_use_when: The question concerns stable policy text. (Inference)
The source system has no read interface. (Inference)

constraints.choice: Pass an OAuth bearer token for an authenticated MCP server.
constraints.combination: Use an allowlist so the model sees only read tools. (Inference)

constraints.choice: Each tool call adds a round trip. (Inference)
constraints.combination: Cache stable tool definitions, but never cache live values. (Inference)

constraints.choice: Use an allowlist to enable only the MCP tools that the route needs.
Describe each tool with the words that users use for the question. (Inference)
constraints.combination: Monitor which tools Claude calls for each question type. (Inference)

components.exam_tie: D3.6. Expect a freshness scenario. The credited answer routes live state to a tool call and keeps documents on the index. (Inference)
components.trap: A faster index refresh looks like the fix for stale values. The index still stores a snapshot, so the answer can lag. (Inference)
components.decision_rule: Route questions about live values to a tool, and route document questions to the index. (Inference)
components.exam_tip: If the scenario names a value that changes in minutes, choose the tool path. (Inference)

decision_flow:
flowchart TD
  A{Question about live state?} -->|Yes| B[Tool call to source system]
  A -->|No| C{Query has exact codes or names?}
  C -->|Yes| D[Keyword match in the mix]
  C -->|No| E[Semantic match]
  D --> F{Mixed query shapes?}
  E --> F
  F -->|Yes| G[Hybrid with rank fusion]
  F -->|No| H[Single matcher]
  G --> I[Rerank merged candidates]
cheatsheet:
flowchart LR
  Q[Query] --> T{Live state}
  T -->|Yes| TL[Tool call]
  T -->|No| M{Code or name}
  M -->|Yes| K[Keyword match]
  M -->|No| S[Semantic match]
  K --> F[Rank fusion]
  S --> F
  F --> RR[Rerank]
